transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Reyes (Solstice Head of Platform), Priya Singh (Solstice SRE), Liam Ortiz (Solstice ML Eng)

Summary (auto): POC to validate latency SLOs under typical Solstice query patterns. Focus on TTFT for chat UI (short-turn latency) and TPOT for long streaming workloads. Need p95 and p99 targets and measurement plan.

--- Transcript body ---
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): okay good afternoon everyone, um I'm Alex with Redwood, i've got Maya the SE with me - she'll drive the technical bits - Jordan, Priya, Liam, thanks for making time. quick confirm, 48 minutes scheduled, is that still fine?
00:12 Jordan (Solstice): yeah that's perfect, thanks. we wanted to get concrete on success criteria and how you recommend we measure TTFT vs, uh, TPOT.
00:20 Maya (Redwood SE): great, so high level we'll cover definitions, target percentiles (p95/p99), workload sizing you should run in the harness, and a measurement plan for the 3-week POC. also note some slight differences in wording that folks use - TTFT = time to first token, TPOT = time per token or per-token throughput.
00:34 Priya (Solstice SRE): quick note: our product has a chat UI and a batch summarization job. chat is our priority for latency - sub-200ms p95 if possible - batch can be higher latency but needs steady TPOT at scale.
00:48 Maya: okay good to know. can you share current observed numbers? that helps us size.
00:51 Priya: we have traces from last month; median TTFT for chat is about 120ms, p95 about 420ms, p99 sits around 1.2s, but those include our nginx + auth overhead. we'll extract pure model-serving deltas.
01:08 Liam (ML Eng): and for batch, we typically run 8k concurrent tokens per second across jobs, so TPOT needs to remain predictable; we care more about cost-per-token there.
01:20 Alex: ok so from a success criteria POV are you looking for absolute numbers you can ship with, or relative improvement vs current stack?
01:28 Jordan: absolute numbers. Execs want a clear SLA we can commit to for the chat feature. ideally p95 under 200ms, p99 under 500ms for the hosted path; fallback to dedicated if we can't hit that.
01:41 Maya: that's ambitious but not impossible; does that p95 target include network and frontend overheads or just the Redwood model-serve time?
01:49 Jordan: we'd like vendor number that includes model-serve and network to our VPC - basically the end-to-end observed from our edge. but we can map the breakdown.
01:58 Maya: okay we'll measure both: 1) client-observed TTFT (end-to-end) and 2) model-server internal TTFT (kernel/kv latency). that'll let us say where the time is spent.
02:10 Priya: good. on TPOT we want per-token in streaming completions, target p95 < 12ms/token and p99 < 20ms/token for the 1-2k concurrent user scenarios. does that align with what you see?
02:23 Maya: yes, for quantized models on Ampere A100 or equivalent, those numbers are reasonable at modest sequence lengths. we'll surface GPU packing and batching impacts.
02:32 Alex: quick clarification on TTFT vs TPOT measurement methodology: TTFT measured from request arrival to first byte of model output; TPOT measured as slope tokens/sec or ms/token after first token, often we report inverse as throughput. we recommend reporting both p95 and p99.
02:48 Liam: for the harness, can you suggest request distributions? our chat workload is 65% short-turn (10-40 tokens), 25% medium (40-150), 10% long (>150). Batch jobs are a different shape - large single requests with ~1k tokens.
03:05 Maya: perfect - include that distribution in the harness. We'll run three phases: cold-cache (no KV or cache), warmed (with prefix caching), and sustained load (to validate throughput and scheduling). also include network emulation to mimic your edge latency (~30ms).
03:22 Jordan: timeline wise, we propose a 3-week POC: week 1 integration + baseline numbers, week 2 benchmark runs + tuning, week 3 final validation + handoff. is that workable?
03:33 Alex: yes that's standard. deliverables: week 1 baseline report, week 2 tuning notes and cluster sizing, week 3 final SLO report and recommendation (hosted vs dedicated).
03:44 Priya: one concern - our security team needs SOC2 and KMS integration details before we start any dedicated runs. we will sign an NDA but they want the doc set.
03:53 Alex: we'll attach our security pack; Maya will send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes as part of the runbook.
03:59 Maya: yep, I'll add that to next steps. also note that for private deployments there's extra setup time - might push some dedicated tests later in the 3-week window.
04:11 Liam: how do you handle variance - like spikes that blow p99 out? do you have fallback routing or model variants?
04:18 Maya: yes. we support smart routing and automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants; in a POC we can exercise that to see graceful degradation. we'll include a test pattern with forced node loss to validate fallbacks.
04:30 Jordan: good. measurement specifics - we need clear definitions in the report: sample size, observation windows, warmup period, and how we compute p95/p99. Please don't give us opaque numbers.
04:41 Maya: agreed. our recommended measurement plan: for each run set - 1) 5 minute warmup, 2) 10 minute steady-state sample, 3) repeat 3 times at each concurrency level. We'll compute p95/p99 on the steady-state windows excluding warmup. we'll also provide CPU/GPU utilization and batching stats per run.
05:02 Priya: what's a realistic concurrency ladder for the harness?
05:06 Maya: start at 10 concurrent chat connections, then 50, 200, 500, and up to 1,000 for stress. for batch, run increasing token injection rates: 500, 1k, 4k, 8k tokens/sec.
05:19 Alex: and we'll annotate runs with sequence-length distributions so we can compare to your production mix.
05:23 Jordan: ok, agreed. what about acceptance criteria? if p95 is below 200ms end-to-end and p99 under 500ms for chat at the 200 concurrent rung, we consider this a pass for hosted. if not, we evaluate dedicated cluster with pinned GPUs and reduced virtualization.
05:39 Liam: also include cost per 1000 tokens for the configs you test - that's a key stakeholder ask.
05:45 Alex: we'll include a cost model: tokens/sec, tokens per-request, and estimated $/1k tokens given throughput and GPU utilization.
05:52 Priya: one more thing - logging and observability. we need structured traces so our SREs can correlate frontend traces with model spans. do you emit trace IDs and exportable spans?
06:02 Maya: yes, we can emit span IDs and provide tracing hooks; we'll include an example Jaeger/Zipkin export in the runbook.
06:09 Jordan: great. on the network side, our VPC sits in us-east-1 and we prefer tests in the same region. can you provision endpoints there?
06:17 Alex: yes we have hosted endpoints in us-east-1; for dedicated/pvt we can spin up a cluster in that region as part of the POC sizing estimate.
06:25 Priya: for the measurement plan doc, please state explicitly how you attribute latency to network vs model. earlier you said you'll measure both model-side and client-side - how will you capture the model-side TTFT?
06:36 Maya: we'll instrument the request lifecycle: ingress timestamp, request queued, batch dispatch, kernel start, first token emitted. model-side TTFT = kernel start to first token; end-to-end TTFT = client send to first byte. We'll provide sample logs and a parser to split those numbers.
06:49 Jordan: sounds thorough. any blockers on our side to start?
06:52 Priya: we'll need to provide sample traces, a small sample dataset, and a short-lived token with network access. security wants the SOC2 doc before we do any dedicated cluster work but hosted runs are fine.
07:05 Alex: action items - I'll share harness, Maya will send SOC2/KMS summary and sizing template. Priya to share traces. We'll reconvene after you've ingested the harness, likely early next week to kick off.
07:19 Jordan: okay let's do that. thanks everyone.
07:22 Alex: thanks all - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep-dive.
07:25 [call ends]

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hears around acronyms (KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash"), and speaker overlap during Q&A.
